message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) belong to very different branches of the mammalian tree:

| Taxonomic level | Lion | Zebra |
|-----------------|------|-------|
| Class | Mammalia | Mammalia |
| Sub‑class | Theria | Theria |
| Infraclass | Eutheria (placentals) | Eutheria |
| Super‑order | Laurasiatheria | Laurasiatheria |
| Order | Carnivora (Feliformia) | Perissodactyla |
| Family | Felidae | Equidae |

Because they diverge at the order level, their most recent common ancestor is the last common ancestor of the two orders **Carnivora** and **Perissodactyla**. That ancestor is a member of the clade **Laurasiatheria**, which split from other placental mammals roughly **70–80 million years ago** during the Late Cretaceous.

So, the common ancestor of a lion and a zebra is the last common ancestor of the Laurasiatherian clade—a placental mammal that lived about 70–80 million years ago.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want a biological answer. The common ancestor of lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) would be a common ancestor in the mammalian lineage. Both are mammals, but lions are felids (family Felidae), zebras are equids (family Equidae). They diverged from a common ancestor in the order Carnivora vs Perissodactyla? Actually lions are in order Carnivora, suborder Feliformia. Zebras are in order Perissodactyla (odd-toed ungulates). So their common ancestor would be a more distant mammalian ancestor, perhaps the last common ancestor of all placental mammals (Eutheria). But maybe they want the last common ancestor of the two species: that would be the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae, which is the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That would be the last common ancestor of the clade that includes both orders, which is the clade of Laurasiatheria? Actually Carnivora and Perissodactyla are both part of the clade Laurasiatheria. So the last common ancestor of lion and zebra would be the last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria, which is a mammal that lived around 70-80 million years ago. But maybe the answer: "The last common ancestor of lions and zebras is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, which lived about 100 million years ago." But more precisely: "The last common ancestor of the two species is the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and the order Perissodactyla, which is a member of the clade Laurasiatheria that lived around 70-80 million years ago." So answer accordingly.
